name: American Telephone & Telegraph

profile.address: 650, Pacific Bell Plaza, Uptown Medical Complex, Hillcrest, San Diego, San Diego County, California, 92103
profile.reading:
The building recorded here as "AT&T Center" is AT&T's landmark central-office complex in the Hillcrest neighborhood of San Diego, a telephone-company facility whose lineage runs back through Pacific Bell to the pre-1984 Bell System, consistent with the deep multi-decade real-estate history the operator, American Telephone & Telegraph (now AT&T Inc.), carries across this registry. Local reporting describes the Hillcrest building as more than 120,000 square feet and roughly a century old, built originally as an emergency communications center -- the source of a basement bomb shelter still on site -- before growing into what is now a central-office switching hub connecting local San Diego callers into the broader public telephone network. Unlike a purpose-built colocation data center marketed to third-party tenants, this is carrier infrastructure: a telephone company's own switching and transmission equipment, housed in a building it has owned and operated across generations of network technology, much of which -- per reporting on the site -- is now described by AT&T's own staff as largely obsolete relative to current network architecture.

The building's most visible feature for decades was a large rooftop microwave relay tower that dominated the Hillcrest skyline; after years of requests from neighborhood groups, AT&T removed it in late 2025 in a three-month teardown, with a company representative citing the equipment having "reached the end of its useful life." That removal has opened a public conversation, reflected in Hillcrest's 2024 community plan, about redeveloping part of the AT&T-owned footprint -- potentially including a sunken garden currently closed to the public -- into housing and civic space, though any such plan remains informal, with only unreleased architectural renderings circulating as of this writing.

AT&T, like other legacy telecom carriers, does not publish technical specifications -- power draw, floor area dedicated to switching gear, redundancy design -- for its central offices; these buildings are operational network infrastructure rather than leasable data center product, so the absence of a spec sheet here reflects the category rather than a gap in reporting. What is publicly documented is the building's age, its origin as mid-twentieth-century emergency communications infrastructure, its continuing role as a live telephone switching center serving San Diego, and the community's active interest in its future footprint as legacy telecom equipment inside it is decommissioned and removed.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] AT&T Inc. is the modern legal and brand successor to the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, originally incorporated on March 3, 1885 and, through its Bell System subsidiaries, the dominant US telephone monopoly for most of the twentieth century until its 1984 antitrust breakup. Following decades of reorganization among the regional Bell operating companies, SBC Communications acquired the reconstituted AT&T Corp for 16 billion dollars in 2005 and renamed itself AT&T Inc., adopting both the historic AT&T name and its New York Stock Exchange ticker, T. AT&T Corp itself continued to exist as a distinct legal subsidiary within the AT&T Inc. corporate family until May 1, 2024, when it was merged into AT&T Enterprises, Inc. and converted to a limited liability company, a technical restructuring driven by New York state law rather than any change in the underlying business. AT&T Inc. is headquartered in Dallas, Texas and files with the SEC under CIK 0000732717. Because AT&Ts corporate lineage runs directly through the American Telephone & Telegraph name, this registry treats a separate operator record under that historical name as the same underlying company rather than an unrelated entity, linked via this record as the canonical, currently branded entry. AT&Ts data center and central office real estate footprint spans decades of Bell System legacy buildings alongside newer facilities built for enterprise, wholesale, and network infrastructure needs, a portfolio distinct in origin from the purpose-built wholesale and hyperscale campuses developed by companies like Vantage or STACK elsewhere in this registry. This facility is recorded under the historic operator name American Telephone and Telegraph in this registry. AT&T Corporation was renamed from American Telephone and Telegraph Company and this facility is treated as the same AT&T entity researched at the operator level. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

American Telephone & Telegraph is the original 1885 incorporated name of the company now operating as AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T, CIK 0000732717). The intermediate entity AT&T Corp, which held this lineage as a subsidiary after SBC Communications' 2005 acquisition and rename to AT&T Inc., was merged into AT&T Enterprises, Inc. and converted to an LLC on May 1, 2024, ending its existence as a separate legal entity. This record is retained as a distinct row per registry policy (no deletion) and cross-linked to the canonical AT&T record via duplicate_of rather than merged.
